title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378F (Memorandum of Producer Company)

content.overview: The memorandum of association of every Producer Company shall state: (a) the name ending with ‘Producer Company Limited’; (b) the State of the registered office; (c) main objects being one or more of the objects in section 378B; (d) names and addresses of subscribers; (e) amount of share capital and division into shares of fixed amount; (f) names, addresses and occupations of the subscriber-producers who shall act as first directors under section 378J(2); (g) that liability of members is limited; (h) against each subscriber’s name the number of shares taken (not less than one); and (i) the States to whose territories the objects extend if not confined to one State.
content.glance: Mandatory contents of the memorandum of a Producer Company, including the name suffix and objects link to s. 378B.
content.study: Section 378F prescribes the compulsory contents of the memorandum. The name must end with ‘Producer Company Limited’. Main objects must be drawn from the list in section 378B. Liability is limited. No subscriber may take fewer than one share. Where objects extend beyond one State, the memorandum must identify those States.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The memorandum must contain the nine particulars listed in s. 378F, including the ‘Producer Company Limited’ name suffix and objects confined to s. 378B.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378F
examples.body: A memorandum that ends the name with ‘Producer Company Limited’ and states objects drawn only from s. 378B satisfies the section.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378F?
hypotheticals.analysis: It fixes the mandatory contents of the memorandum, including the name form and the objects link to s. 378B.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the words ‘Producer Company Limited’ from the name.
misconceptions.correction: Those words are mandatory last words of the name under s. 378F(a).
